 The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Revision Case No.316 Of 2011

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: O R D E R:

The present Criminal Revision Case is filed against the judgment dated 08.02.2011 in Criminal Appeal No.87 of 2007 on the file of the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Nalgonda (for short, "the appellate Court") in confirming the judgment dated 24.07.2007 in C.C.No.645 of 2011 on the file of the learned Special Judicial First Class Magistrate (Prohibition and Excise Offences), Nalgonda (for short, "the trial Court").
2.
Heard Mr. Srinivas, learned counsel representing Mr. Kowturu Pavan Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Vizarath Ali, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent State.
Perused the record.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 10.12.1998, the de facto complainant namely P. Vasantha,
Accounts Officer, at R.M.O. Officer, Nalgonda stated that the petitioner/accused, while working as Shroff at R.P.O., APSRTC, Nalgonda, involved in embezzlement of money by drawing unauthorized amounts.
It was detected at the time of reconciliation of the Bank Statement.
On enquiry, it was found that the accused drew an amount of Rs.20,913.50/- instead of Rs.2,913.50/- vide cheque No.339587 dated 20.12.1997.
He drew an amount of Rs.18,500/- instead of Rs.8,500/- vide cheque No.339596 dated 02.01.1998.
He also drew an amount of Rs.20,600/- instead of Rs.2,600/- vide cheque No.7155 dated 23.10.1999 and the accused was placed under suspension w.e.f. 07.12.1998 for his misdeeds.
Basing on the said facts, the present case was registered.

4. The trial Court vide judgment cited supra found the accused guilty for the offences under Sections 408, 420 and 468 of I.P.C. and he was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years for the offence under Section 408 of I.P.C and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to undergo simple imprisonment for three months.
5.

The trial Court also sentenced the accused to undergo simple imprisonment for two years for the offence under Section 468 of I.P.C. and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to suffer imprisonment for three months.
He was further sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for two years for the offence under Section 420 of I.P.C. and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to undergo three months imprisonment.
The sentence imposed for the aforesaid offences was directed to run concurrently.
Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner preferred an appeal.

sentences.text: 6. The appellate Court vide judgment cited supra, dismissed the appeal confirming the judgment passed by the trial Court.
Assailing the same, the present Revision.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the trial Court as well as the appellate Court failed to appreciate the evidence available on record in proper perspective and concurrently found the petitioner guilty of the alleged offences.
Therefore, he seeks to set aside the impugned judgment.

8. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that the both the Courts upon careful scrutiny of the evidence available on record rightly passed their respective judgments and the interference of this Court is unwarranted.
Therefore, he seeks to dismiss the Revision.

9. On behalf of the prosecution, the trial Court examined PWs.1 to 10 and marked Exs.P1 to P127,
MOs.1 and 2.
On behalf of the defence, none were examined and Exs.D1 to D4 were marked.
Upon careful scrutiny of the oral and documentary evidence, the learned Judge, trial Court observed that,
as per the evidence of PW1, the accused was entrusted with certain sum of money, on different dates, for remitting it into the account of APSRTC.
But the accused remitted lesser amounts into credit of the APSRTC and drew excess money wrongfully.

The prosecution proved that the accused remitted lesser money and drew excess money by adding numerals and writings on the cheques, on different dates, which was clear from the documentary evidence i.e., books of accounts and the mode of keeping such accounts.

10. The ocular evidence of PW1 itself speaks that on verification of the cheque issue register, she found that the accused drew an amount of Rs.20,913.50/- vide cheque No.339587 dated 20.12.1997 instead of Rs.2,913.50/-, Rs.18,500/- vide cheque No.339596 dated 02.01.1998 instead of Rs.8,500/- and Rs.20,600/- vide cheque No.7155 dated 23.1.1999 instead of Rs.2,600/-.
Ex P99 is the entry in the cheque issue register dated 20.12.1997 relating to Ex P1.
Ex P100 is the entry in the cheque issue register dated 02.01.1998 relating to Ex P13.

Ex P101 is the entry in the cheque issue register dated 23.01.1998 relating to cheque Ex P2.
11.
On verification, PW1 found that on 16.09.1999 the accused was asked to remit an amount for Rs.3,083/- but he deposited Rs.83/- only and the difference is Rs.3,000/-.
On 22.09.1997 he was asked to remit an amount of Rs.1,305/- but he deposited only Rs.5/- and difference is Rs.1,300/-.
Ex P32 is the counter foil dated 16.09.1997 for an amount of Rs.3,083/-.

Moreover, on 03.10.1997,
accused was to deposit an amount of Rs.67,795/- but he deposited Rs.7,795/-.
Ex P102 is the entry in cash book dated 03.10.1997 relating to Ex P34 which is the counter foil.
12. PW1, in her ocular evidence stated that all the details pertaining to the cheques as to how accused has drawn more amounts and how he remitted lesser amounts when he was entrusted with cash.

All the documents, i.e., counter foils which are marked as Ex P32 dated 03.10.1997 to Ex P49 disclosed the amount to be remitted into account of APSRTC bearing No.2738 and Exs.P15 to 31 shows that the amounts remitted by the accused.
The difference in the amount which was to be remitted was clear vide Exs.P32 to P49 and Exs.P15 to 31.
Therefore, the prosecution clearly proved that the accused was entrusted with cash for remitting but he remitted lesser amounts which clearly shows the dishonest intention on his part.

sentences.text: PW3, in his ocular evidence, stated that the accused usually used to go to the bank to draw the funds, remit the amounts and transfer the amounts from one to another.

The evidence of PW6 also supports the prosecution case that on 03.01.1999 police recorded the statement of accused in his presence, where the accused did not deposit the cheque amounts, misappropriated some amounts and the accused himself confessed that he purchased a Colour TV, a Car and a Washing Machine.

From the evidence of PWs.1, 3 and 6, it was clear that the accused misappropriated the amounts and committed the offence of the criminal breach of trust.
14.
The evidence of PW1, Vasantha and PW3 also disclosed that the accused remitted lesser amounts and drew excess amount which caused variations in the cash deposits of APSRTC.
This shows that the accused with a dishonest intention, to gain unlawfully, misappropriated the property to a tune of Rs.6,85,700/- and committed the offence of Section 420 of I.P.C.
The evidence of PW1 was corroborated by the documentary evidence with regard to the entries made in the cheque book issue register.

Therefore, the prosecution proved that the accused upon entrustment of property,
misappropriated it and converted to his own use.

15. The case of the prosecution clearly shows that the accused forged the original cheques, original vouchers and original cheques containing his signatures on one leaf of the cheque intending that it shall be used for the purpose of cheating the bank authorities and thus, proved that the accused committed the offence under Section 467 of I.P.C.
16.
The evidence of PW2 showed that the accused by adding numerals etc. on the cheques forged them with a dishonest intention to gain wrongfully.
The trial Court noticed that the evidence of PW1 is supported by evidence of PWs.2 and 6.
The accused himself confessed in the presence of PW6 that he misappropriated the amounts and converted for his own use which is quite evident from MOs.1 and 2.

Thus, the trial Court found that the prosecution successfully proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections.408, 420 and 467 of I.P.C. beyond all reasonable doubt and rendered the judgment cited supra.
17.

In the appeal, the appellate Court observed that as per the evidence of PW1, during her tenure at Nalgonda, the petitioner worked as Shroff in their Office and he was in the work of depositing the cash in the bank and encash the cheques from the Bank.
The evidence of PW2, who was an expert in giving opinion stated that the signatures, initials and writings of the petitioner in the cheques and vouchers are proved.

If really, the petitioner was innocent and if he was not entrusted with any money transactions by PW1, the signatures and writings on the cheques and counterfoils should not have tallied with that of the petitioner.
But, on comparison, the signatures of the petitioner on the leave letters were found to be tallying with the writings in Exs.P1 to P14 cheques and other documents.

18. Therefore, the appellate Court also found that the evidence adduced by the prosecution is sufficient to prove that the petitioner was entrusted with the work of depositing and encashing cheques with the Bank and during that period, the petitioner misappropriated the cheques and deposited lesser amounts through vouchers.

Thus, the prosecution proved that there was entrustment of property to the petitioner and misappropriation of funds by the petitioner with P. Subramanyiyam, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197672267/

sentences.text: dishonest intention to cause wrongful loss to the Corporation.
Therefore, the appellate Court dismissed the appeal confirming the conviction imposed against the petitioner while reducing the sentence therein.

19. A perusal of the record shows that this Court vide order dated 11.02.2011 suspended the operation of sentence imposed against the petitioner by the learned District and Sessions Judge,
Nalgonda and enlarged him on bail on executing a bond for an amount of Rs.10,000/- by him with two sureties each for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
Thereafter, the matter underwent several adjournments.

20. In the present case on hand, both the Courts have concurrently held that the petitioner was guilty of the offences punishable under Sections.408, 468 and 420 of I.P.C., which finding, in my considered view, does not call for interference, in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under Section 397 Cr.P.C.
21.

Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel, upon considering the fact that the petitioner suffered mental agony and hardship during the course of litigation before the trial Court as well as the appellate Court and as thirteen long years have elapsed from the date of filing this Revision, this Court in inclined to take a lenient view and reduced the sentence imposed against the petitioner to the period of imprisonment already undergone by him.

22. The petitioner is directed to deposit an amount of Rs.50,000/- each for the offences under Sections 408, 420 and 467 of I.P.C., which comes to Rs.1,50,000/- in total, to the credit of the trial Court, within a period of three months from today.
Failing which, the petitioner is directed to undergo simple imprisonment for six months each for the offences under Sections 408, 420 and 467 of I.P.C.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
23. Except the above modification, the Criminal Revision Case in all other aspects, stands dismissed.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
